root_cause: Aspose.Email.LowCode.FolderOutputHandler does not implement IDisposable. After ConvertToHtml completes (task returns), FolderOutputHandler retains an open exclusive write handle on the output HTML file. When the harness calls File.ReadAllText() to check HTML content, Windows rejects the open with: IOException: The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process.

fix.approach: Force GC to finalize FolderOutputHandler before reading output files
fix.pattern: Let handler variable go out of scope, then call GC.Collect() + GC.WaitForPendingFinalizers() + GC.Collect()
fix.code_change: Wrapped handler in inner scope block; called GC.Collect/WaitForPendingFinalizers/GC.Collect before Directory.GetFiles

tests: ConvertToHtml: PASS (1 file, 2092 bytes, contains HTML tags)

note_on_generated_examples: The Email LowCode generated example (PR merged in Email/Slides Activation Sprint) uses ConvertToMsg pattern, which does NOT trigger the file-lock. The file-lock only affects the harness output validation step, not the generated example execution. The published example is unaffected.
verdict: EMAIL_HARNESS_5_5_ALL_PASS — ConvertToHtml file-lock fixed via GC.Collect pattern. Harness now 5/5. FolderOutputHandler does not implement IDisposable; GC finalization is the only available release mechanism.
